key_insight: Quantum Density Functional Theory reduces qubit requirements to O(log₂ N) for N orbitals by solving a non-interacting Kohn–Sham reference problem.
engineering_relevance: Pairing qubit-efficient algorithms with programmable photonic hardware offers a route toward near-term molecular simulation with reduced qubit overhead.
method: Reformulate electronic structure using a non-interacting Kohn–Sham reference system.
Use ensemble variational quantum eigensolving to minimize energy in a ground- and first-excited-state subspace.
Encode qubits on a photonic platform combining a deterministic quantum-dot single-photon source and a programmable integrated circuit.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimental validation on lithium hydride (LiH), evaluating molecular ground- and first-excited-state properties without providing numerical accuracy metrics.
watch_item: Logarithmic qubit scaling does not establish total computational advantage; larger-system performance and accuracy remain to be demonstrated.
paper_title: Quantum Simulation of Electronic Structure using Quantum Density Functional Theory on a Programmable Integrated Photonic Circuit
